why:
The log is what gets read when something has already gone wrong, so its quiet failures are the expensive ones: a line that will not parse takes the record either side of it with it, and a run several processes wrote becomes unreadable at exactly the moment it was supposed to earn its keep. It is also an assertion surface - the launch smoke check and the perf harness both read it - so its shape is a contract rather than a formatting preference.

Two properties, both here as data. Identity comes first (when, how precisely, how bad, who, what) because those are what a reader scans by, and payload fields are sorted so the same code twice produces the same bytes. And nothing in a payload may break out of its line: this log carries terminal bytes, which are full of quotes, escapes and control characters.

cases.name: identity first, payload sorted
cases.why: The key order is what makes a raw log readable without a tool, and the sort is what makes two runs of the same code diffable. Fields arriving in hash order would make every run look different from the last.

cases.name: a record with no fields is still a whole object
cases.why: Most records carry only their identity. A trailing comma or a dangling brace here would make the commonest line in the file the one that does not parse.

cases.name: a payload cannot break out of its line
cases.why: Terminal bytes are exactly what this log carries, and they are full of escapes, quotes and control characters. One unescaped newline splits a record into two unparseable halves - and it would do so only for the records describing whatever went wrong, which are the ones being read.

cases.name: a field name is escaped like a value
cases.why: Field names come from call sites rather than from a fixed list, so nothing structurally prevents one containing a quote. An escaped value beside an unescaped key would produce a line that parses as something other than what was logged.

cases.name: the event name is escaped too
cases.why: Event names are dotted identifiers by convention, not by enforcement. The convention is worth relying on for grepping and not for parsing.
